terra.problem: It says the vines are already stripped. The comparison specifies no cluster to eat and no early fig, not that all the vines have been stripped.
“Micah finds nothing” turns the comparison into an actual search and goes beyond the missing cluster and early fig.
It treats Micah’s comparison as a vineyard with nothing left for him. The text specifies no cluster to eat and no early fig.
It states that people are using an actual net on one another. The passage says they hunt one another with a net but does not establish that a literal net is being used.
It states that the leaders’ conduct is why Micah is troubled. The passage does not explicitly give that reason.
It states that the leaders want payment to bend what they do. The passage says they demand a bribe, but does not specify what they intend to do for it.
It adds that nobody stops to question the conspiracy. The passage does not say that.
It says Micah shows how the wrongdoing spreads. The verse describes them conspiring together, not a process of it spreading.
It calls the woman the closest person there is. The text says she lies in the person’s arms but does not rank their closeness.
“It’s not out in the streets. It’s inside the home” presents the problem as confined to the home, although Micah also describes wrongdoing among people more broadly.
It says Micah does not go looking for new friends. The text does not say whether he does; it says he will look to the LORD and wait.
